candidates.title: Guardian foreclosure blocks staging/acceptance of a finished tournament, so the settled state's outputs are never accepted
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 DaveConsensus (cartesi-rollups/contracts) with rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application
candidates.role: Referee model (deployed referee), per AUDIT.md component table
candidates.description: The only path that adds an epoch's outputs Merkle root to `_outputsMerkleRoots` (the set `isOutputsMerkleRootValid` reads) is stageTournamentResult followed by acceptStagedTournamentResult, and both revert once the Application is foreclosed. Application.foreclose() is callable at any time by the guardian. So, after the root tournament has a ROOT_WINNER (the settled state per A5: the last leaf of the winning claim), or after staging but before the claim staging period ends, the guardian can make the winner's outputs root permanently unprovable: no function settles a staged result after foreclosure, and executeOutput of those outputs reverts with InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot. Outputs of roots accepted earlier stay executable (executeOutput and isOutputsMerkleRootValid are not gated).
candidates.trigger: The guardian address of WithdrawalConfig calls Application.foreclose() after the tournament finished (or after stageTournamentResult) and before acceptStagedTournamentResult.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on any deployment created by DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp with a non-zero guardian; it needs no particular machine state, only the timing window between a tournament's end and acceptance (at least the claim staging period unless all sentries agree).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Possibly: the guardian is a privileged role the deployment configures, not one of the adversaries of section 7, and foreclosure is a deliberate emergency feature; if triage reads the guardian as a trusted part of the deployment, the trigger is 'the deployment violates A5' and section 8 excludes 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it'. Here the implementation of the referee model (Dave's contracts) is itself what lets a party stop acceptance, so the exception may apply. 2 Role: Dave contracts = referee model, rated 'as if a deployed referee had it' (section 3). 3 High/Medium cases: none matches. 4 Critical? A5: 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' If 'no party' includes the guardian, the referee stops accepting outputs of a settled state -> Critical. 5 Otherwise Low (design trust assumption, documented foreclosure semantics). The deciding fact: whether the threat model treats the guardian as a party the deployment trusts (then out of scope/Low) or as 'any party' under A5 (then Critical).
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Critical under the reading that A5's 'no party' covers the guardian)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 does not break (no wrong state or wrong output is accepted); A5's completeness clause does: valid outputs that a tournament-settled state commits to become permanently unexecutable at a privileged party's discretion.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: both settlement functions carry notForeclosed(_APP_CONTRACT); there is no un-foreclose or post-foreclosure settlement path; Application.foreclose is onlyGuardian notForeclosed.
candidates.test_idea: On the harness chain with the released Dave build: deploy via DaveAppFactory with guardian=G, add an input whose app emits a voucher, let the honest player win the tournament, call stageTournamentResult, then have G call foreclose(); assert that acceptStagedTournamentResult succeeds and that executeOutput of the voucher with its valid proof succeeds (required by A5). Today both revert -> exit 1.

candidates.title: Outputs-root extraction (machine validity proof) is compiled against machine-solidity-step v0.15.0 constants, not the deployment's step
candidates.component: cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 LibMachineValidityProof/LibLeafProof/CanonicalMachine as linked into Dave's DaveConsensus
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/library/LibMachineValidityProof.sol (EmulatorCompat.isYieldedManualWith, EmulatorConstants.HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_ACCEPTED from cartesi-machine-solidity-step-0.15.0); bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/common/CanonicalMachine.sol (IFLAGS_Y_ADDRESS, HTIF_TOHOST_ADDRESS, TX_BUFFER_START, LOG2_MAX_OUTPUTS, LOG2_DATA_BLOCK_SIZE from step 0.15.0); bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/foundry.toml remapping `cartesi-machine-solidity-step-0.15.0/=.../dependencies/cartesi-machine-solidity-step-0.15.0/`
candidates.description: DaveConsensus._validateMachine authenticates iflags_Y, htif_tohost and the first tx-buffer word through LibMachineValidityProof, whose addresses, HTIF field masks/shifts, accepted-reason value, output-tree height and leaf size come from machine-solidity-step v0.15.0, while the deployment's state transition (step, reset, delivery) comes from the step regenerated from audit/prt2 (v0.17.0-test1 lineage; CM_MARCHID 23). The A5 extraction therefore interprets the settled state with the layout of another protocol version. I compared every constant it uses with the regenerated EmulatorConstants.sol and with the in-tree emulator: IFLAGS_Y_ADDRESS 0x308, HTIF_TOHOST_ADDRESS 0x330, AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_START 0x60800000, ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_OUTPUT_COUNT 63, HTIF_DEV/CMD/REASON masks and shifts, RX_ACCEPTED=1, Memory.LOG2_LEAF=5, and AccessLogs word extraction all coincide today, so no wrong extraction exists on audit/prt2. The defect is that nothing ties them: a layout change of these registers in the emulator would leave the on-chain extraction silently reading other words, and the deployed verifier code is not built from the audited source.
candidates.trigger: None at present; becomes live when a protocol version moves iflags_Y, htif_tohost, the tx buffer or the HTIF encoding while Dave keeps the pinned rollups-contracts.
candidates.reachability: Today the constants match (checked), so no state triggers a wrong extraction.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion applies to a constant mismatch inside the referee model. 2 Role: referee model (Dave contracts as deployed referee). 3 High/Medium cases: closest is 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source' (R13: 'the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source'); the validity-check code is built from step v0.15.0 sources rather than the audited ones, but its behavior matches. A6: 'Every verifier, the uarch program fixed on-chain, and every honest operator in a deployment implements the same state transition function (R13)' is not violated today because the values are equal. 4 Critical: no, no reachable wrong extraction. 5 Low: latent version-mixing hazard.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (High only if triage counts building on-chain referee code from a different step release as the R13 reproducibility case)
candidates.threat_to_goal: No current threat; a future layout change would make the referee extract an outputs root from the wrong words (accepting outputs the settled state does not commit to, or refusing valid ones), breaking A5 without any test in the emulator noticing.
candidates.evidence: Ran lua5.4 with the in-tree cartesi module: get_reg_address(iflags_Y)=0x308, htif_tohost=0x330, AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_START=0x60800000, ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_OUTPUT_COUNT=63, RX_ACCEPTED=1, MARCHID=23; grepped the same constants in step-0.15.0 EmulatorConstants.sol and regenerated-patched EmulatorConstants.sol: equal. Read Dave's foundry.toml remapping.
candidates.test_idea: A Lua test that reads both EmulatorConstants.sol files (the one Dave links for LibMachineValidityProof and the regenerated one) and the cartesi module, and asserts that DaveConsensus's validity check is compiled from the deployment's step (e.g., same file hash/remapping); exits 1 while LibMachineValidityProof resolves to step-0.15.0.

candidates.title: `rollup` CLI ignores load/save errors of the outputs Merkle tree and rewrites /tmp/merkle.dat non-atomically; a short or missing file silently resets the tree
candidates.component: machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1: sys-utils/rollup/rollup.cpp and libcmt cmt_merkle_load/cmt_util_write_whole_file
candidates.location: mgt/sys-utils/rollup/rollup.cpp class rollup ctor/dtor (cmt_rollup_load_merkle/cmt_rollup_save_merkle return values discarded, path /tmp/merkle.dat); mgt/sys-utils/libcmt/src/merkle.c cmt_merkle_load (reads straight into the live struct, then returns -EINVAL on a short file); mgt/sys-utils/libcmt/src/util.c cmt_util_write_whole_file (fopen "wb" truncates, then fwrite/fclose, no temp file+rename)
candidates.description: Shell-style applications (the documented `rollup notice|voucher|accept` flow, used by the manual's rolling calculator and the harness valid-template echo app) keep the outputs tree only in /tmp/merkle.dat: each `rollup` process loads it in its constructor and saves it in its destructor, ignoring both return codes. If the save fails after the truncation (ENOSPC/EIO on the second write, or the process is killed mid-write), the file is empty or partial; the next `rollup accept` then either loads nothing (tree pristine, leaf_count 0) or a half-overwritten struct (cmt_merkle_load copies the bytes into the live tree before checking the length), and libcmt writes to the tx buffer an outputs Merkle root that does not commit to the outputs accepted before. The command that emitted the output still exits 0, and so does accept. Effects: outputs emitted earlier lose their place in later roots, and new outputs reuse indices already marked in Application._executed, so a valid output of a later settled root can be refused as OutputNotReexecutable.
candidates.trigger: An input (or accumulated input data) that makes the guest's write of /tmp/merkle.dat fail or be interrupted after truncation; also any app-side cleanup of /tmp.
candidates.reachability: Not demonstrated. In the steady state the rewrite reuses the block freed by the truncation, so plain disk-full rarely triggers it; reaching it from an input against a correctly designed app needs a failure between truncate and write (filesystem error, signal). Needs a prover to find an input-driven path (e.g., tmpfs page accounting under memory pressure created by the app's own legitimate data).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Section 8 excludes 'Guest software that an input can subvert, as long as R7 and R8 hold, other than the defects that section 3 puts in scope' and applications not correctly designed; section 3 puts in scope 'A defect that lets an input make such an application deviate from the rollup interface'. 2 Role: guest software (machine-guest-tools). 3 High/Medium: none. 4 Critical if an input to a correctly designed app using `rollup` as documented can trigger the failed save: section 3 'A defect that lets an input make such an application deviate from the rollup interface is Critical, as an R7 deviation in the rx buffer, the tx buffer and the yield interface'; the deviation is the definition 'When it accepts, it leaves in the tx buffer the outputs Merkle root of every output it accepted'. 5 Otherwise Low ('Any other defect in them is Low').
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Critical if an input-driven trigger exists)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not let a wrong state settle; makes a correctly designed application publish an outputs root that omits accepted outputs, so A5 completeness (every output the application accepted is provable) fails for that application.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of the pinned tag (bare git clone of v0.18.1-test1 into scratch).
candidates.test_idea: Build a valid template from the guest-tools rootfs whose app emits a notice with `rollup notice` and accepts with `rollup accept`; between two inputs make /tmp/merkle.dat unwritable or truncated through the app's documented storage behaviour, then assert that the tx-buffer root after accept equals the frontier root of all emitted outputs, or that `rollup` exits non-zero. Today the root silently becomes the empty-tree root -> exit 1.

candidates.title: libcmt cmt_merkle_push_back loses the full-tree root at the 2^63-th output
candidates.description: With CMT_MERKLE_TREE_HEIGHT=63 and leaf_count = 2^63-1, push_back combines with every level and never stores the result (the loop ends without `break`), then sets leaf_count = 2^63. get_root_hash sees no bit set in levels 0..62 and returns the pristine root, so the root after the last possible output is the empty-tree root instead of the full tree.
candidates.reachability: Needs 2^63 outputs, each costing guest mcycles; no deployment is sized for that, so it is practically unreachable, though not excluded by the dispute constants alone.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs' is about operator cost, not this; no exclusion fits exactly. 2 Role: guest software. 3 None. 4 Not Critical in practice: no input sequence within any deployment's sizing reaches 2^63 outputs. 5 Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None in practice; documents an edge where the outputs root would stop committing to the outputs.
candidates.test_idea: Unit test of libcmt with a cmt_merkle_t whose leaf_count is set to 2^63-1 and whose state holds known subtree roots; push one leaf and assert get_root_hash equals the reference full-tree root (e.g., from cartesi.hash-tree frontier).
